user_stories.story: As a user creating a log, I can enter a description of 1 to 200 characters, and longer ones are rejected with a clear message.
As a user editing a log, the same 1..200 rule applies, and a rejected edit leaves the log unchanged.
As a user in the browser, the description fields stop accepting input at 200 characters and API errors tell me what to do next.

acceptance_criteria.c: POST /api/logs with a description of 1 character (after trim) succeeds.
POST with exactly 200 characters succeeds; with 201 returns 422 and detail "description must be at most 200 characters"; nothing is stored.
POST with 200 characters plus leading/trailing spaces succeeds and the stored description is the trimmed 200 characters.
POST with whitespace-only or missing description still returns 422 "description is required and cannot be blank".
A rejected PUT (201 chars or blank) leaves the stored log byte-for-byte unchanged (verified by re-reading it).
The 200 limit is a named constant in backend/models.py beside the other limits, and routes.py uses it.
textarea#description in index.html and the textarea created by the inline edit form in app.js both carry maxlength="200".
ERROR_HINTS in app.js has an entry for the new detail, yielding "Couldn't your log: description must be at most 200 characters. Shorten your description to 200 characters or fewer and try again."

All 112 existing tests pass (any test that sent more than 200 characters is updated and listed in the report), plus the new tests; test_real_paths_untouched passes; real logs.db and uploads/ are never touched (temp paths only).

assumptions.a: Length is Python len() of the trimmed string (Unicode code points), per the request.
Browser maxlength counts UTF-16 code units, so emoji may hit the limit slightly earlier in the browser than on the server. Recorded, not reconciled.
No visual counter, no minlength attribute, no style.css change, no docs/Docker changes, no new files.
Edited files: backend/routes.py, backend/models.py, backend/tests/test_logs.py, frontend/index.html, frontend/app.js.

edge_cases.e: Exactly 200 and 201 characters, with and without surrounding whitespace.
Over-long description that is padded: only the trimmed length counts.
Multi-code-point characters (emoji) counted by code points on the server.
Blank check runs before the length check, so whitespace-only keeps the existing message.

risks.risk: Existing tests sending descriptions over 200 characters will fail until updated.
The ERROR_HINTS key must match the server detail string exactly, or the hint silently won't show.
Browser and server length counts differ for non-BMP characters.

spec.dependencies: Existing files only; no new packages.
spec.self_critique: Every story maps to a criterion and every criterion is observable. The biggest unknown is how many existing tests use more than 200 characters, and the implementer must list them. The ERROR_HINTS matching mechanism (exact or substring) was not inspected.
